overall_summary: Initial tests with hyper-niche 'self respect' digital clutter actions yielded very low views (under 50), while out-of-niche family and universal relationship emotional shorts (Maa, Papa, Call someone you love) clearly outperformed with 100+ to 220+ views. This indicates the audience prefers broader emotional family/relationship connection over repetitive micro-actions of digital deleting.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'माँ जब पूछती है…' (215 views) and 'आज किसी अपने को Call कर लेना…' (220 views) performed significantly better than digital deletion self-respect tropes.
winning_patterns.action: Pivot the core content slightly broader to include relatable interpersonal relationships and unsaid words alongside self-respect.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple variations of clearing storage, deleting archives, or removing chat pins (e.g., cuKSS0gHyt0, hT4EGP69mRw) stalled below 15-40 views.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid overusing tech-cleanup metaphors and focus more on real emotional conversations and unexpressed feelings.
